narrative.overview: Código Real reads as a serious developer tool that happens to be a landing page, not a marketing page pretending to be a tool. The dominant register is a deep, solid-dark IDE canvas (#0b0f19) at the top (nav + hero + Playground) and bottom (CTA + footer), with a single light section in the middle ("Elige tu camino" / tags) that functions as a paper interlude between two dark bookends — a deliberate split confirmed by the shipped structure, not a stray inconsistency. There are no decorative gradients on the canvas itself: color is restrained to thin slate borders and one reused indigo→violet accent, spent only on the hero's headline span and primary CTA gradients. The Playground is the one place ornament gives way to function — it embeds the real Monaco Editor (VS Code's engine, loaded from CDN) with a live srcdoc iframe preview, so the product's central claim ("this is a real editor, not a mockup") is load-bearing to the visual system, not just copy. Language "ficha" cards break this restraint on purpose: each gets a flat, pale tint of its own language's brand color (HTML orange, CSS blue, JS yellow) as a full card background inside the light middle section — the one place the world intentionally turns colorful, echoing familiar language-brand hues rather than the site's own indigo accent.
keyCharacteristics: Solid dark canvas at rest; no gradients, no glow, no glassmorphism.
One accent gradient (indigo → violet), spent only on gated moments: hero headline span, primary CTA buttons, primary icon badges.
A light "paper" section in the middle of an otherwise dark page, holding the three per-language ficha cards and the tag chips.
Soft rounded geometry throughout (rounded-xl/rounded-2xl); never sharp corners, never heavy shadows.
Hand-authored inline SVG icons only; no icon fonts, no emoji.
A real code editor (Monaco) and a real iframe preview are first-class visual citizens, not screenshots.

rules.name: The One Gradient Rule
rules.body: The indigo→violet gradient appears in exactly three roles across the page — hero headline span, primary CTA backgrounds, and small accent icon badges — never as a section background, never as a border, never repeated as a second competing gradient.

rules.name: The Ficha Rule
rules.body: A language's brand color (HTML/CSS/JS) is only ever used as a pale card tint plus a solid small icon badge and CTA button inside a language card. It never appears as the site's own accent, and the site's own accent never appears inside a ficha card.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: No small uppercase/eyebrow label sits above any heading anywhere on the built page (hero, section headers, CTA banner). Every H1/H2 carries its own weight without a kicker; do not add one to a future section.

rules.name: The One-Face Rule
rules.body: Inter is the only UI/display face; JetBrains Mono is the only monospace face. Do not introduce a third family for "personality" — the tool character comes from restraint, not from typographic variety.

rules.name: The Border-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth between adjacent panels (nav, cards, Playground panes, footer) is conveyed with a 1px slate border, never a box-shadow. Reserve shadow for the single most important object on a given viewport.

dos: Do spend the indigo→violet accent only on the hero headline span, primary CTA gradients, and small icon badges — never as a section or card background.
Do use a 1px slate border to separate adjacent panels; reach for shadow-2xl only for the page's single most important object (the Playground).
Do keep language-brand colors (HTML/CSS/JS) confined to their own ficha cards and tab icons; never let them leak into the site's own accent role.
Do use JetBrains Mono only for literal code or code-like tokens (tag chips, the editor); Inter for everything else.
Do keep corners soft (rounded-lg to rounded-2xl); never introduce a sharp-cornered element.
donts: Don't add a kicker/eyebrow label above any heading. None exists in the shipped build; the H1 and section H2s carry their own weight unassisted.
Don't introduce icon fonts, emoji, or third-party icon packages. Every icon is a hand-authored inline SVG in Icon.astro.
Don't add a second accent gradient or a second brand hue outside the indigo-violet pair and the three fixed language colors.
Don't apply drop shadows to cards or buttons for "depth"; the system conveys separation with borders, reserving shadow for the Playground alone.
